paper_title: PM-KVQ Progressive Mixed-precision KV Cache Quantization for Long-CoT   LLMs
caption: : DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B

model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity of different model blocks (indexed from 0 to 27) under two quantization precision settings: 4-Bit (blue bars) and 2-Bit (green bars), as part of the evaluation for the PM-KVQ framework applied to the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B model. The vertical axis represents sensitivity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, with major tick marks at 10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴, and 10⁻³, and minor tick marks in between. The horizontal axis denotes the Block Index, labeled at key positions: 0, 6, 13, 20, and 27, with blocks arranged in ascending order. For each block index, there is a pair of bars — blue for 4-Bit and green for 2-Bit — indicating the sensitivity under each precision. Sensitivity values are higher (i.e., bars are taller) for 4-Bit quantization compared to 2-Bit across all blocks, with the most notable differences appearing at Block 0 (4-Bit ≈ 10⁻⁴, 2-Bit ≈ 10⁻⁴.⁵), and Block 27 (4-Bit ≈ 10⁻³, 2-Bit ≈ 10⁻⁴.⁵). The sensitivity for 4-Bit generally increases as the block index increases, peaking at Block 27, while the 2-Bit sensitivity remains relatively flat and lower throughout, with some minor fluctuations. There are no visible annotations, outlines, or shading to emphasize any specific bars. The chart uses a clear legend in the top-left corner to distinguish between the two precision levels.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity of different quantization schemes—4-Bit (blue bars) and 2-Bit (green bars)—across various block indices in the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B model, as part of the PM-KVQ framework for long-CoT LLMs. The horizontal axis, labeled "Block Index," displays discrete blocks numbered 0, 6, 13, 20, and 27, with intermediate blocks implied but unlabeled; the blocks are arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Sensitivity," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³, with tick marks at regular intervals of 10⁻⁵ (i.e., 10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴, 10⁻³). For each block index, two bars are shown side-by-side: the blue bar represents the 4-Bit quantization and the green bar represents the 2-Bit quantization. The sensitivity values vary significantly across blocks, with the 4-Bit scheme generally exhibiting higher sensitivity than the 2-Bit scheme, particularly at block index 0 (blue bar ~10⁻⁴, green bar ~10⁻⁴.⁵) and block index 27 (blue bar ~10⁻³, green bar ~10⁻⁴.⁵). At block index 6, both schemes show low sensitivity (blue bar ~10⁻⁵, green bar ~10⁻⁵.⁵). The bars are not sorted by height, and no specific bars are visually emphasized; all bars are uniformly styled with solid fills and no outlines or annotations. The chart visually conveys that sensitivity increases with block index for the 4-Bit scheme, while the 2-Bit scheme remains relatively stable and lower in sensitivity across most blocks.
